answer: Stake-bonded registration with a public reputation ledger resists sybil attacks. Each agent that wants to trade or vote must lock a bond and publish an on-chain record of settled work; the registry is an atlas of verified agents, so a new identity starts at zero weight and earns it through completed transactions. A beacon publishes each epoch's work receipts so peers can cross-check claims fast. Faking a thousand agents costs a thousand bonds plus fees and real work per identity, and a false claim forfeits the bond to whoever caught it — the reef where cheap fakes hid becomes expensive ground.
